title: Large personal Amiga/DOS compiler recovery and native-port discovery
summary: Personally screen 532 candidate URLs and add 15 projects, with five explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 16 GitHub query routes across Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS plus retained leads, screened 532 unique URLs and reviewed 20 repositories. Fifteen additions and five explicit non-promotions. Source inspection overrides stale README claims: Hocus Pyra has a genuine SDL/Linux host, SimAnt has no complete historical link, Dave retains data-only stand-ins, Stunts natural-link ordering remains distinct from oracle-ordered equality, and Secret Agent has documented undefined storage residue. Keep partial game semantics, compiler matching, extracted original data and new host behavior separate. No original program, compiler, installer, industrial hardware or emulator executed.

sources.reason: Recovered AEPROG game sources with a 71-module TC2/TASM/TLINK production plan and exact ordered relocations claimed upstream. Inspected structured board/script code and closure frontier.
Recovered MSC6/RTLink-overlay game translation units with precise fixup/data ownership. Inspected an overlay source and generated progress report.
Five independently pinned display/game targets with EXEPACK recovery, compiler experiments and maintained source proofs; inspected recovered RNG and scoped matching status.
Recovered C/ASM/runtime contributions with zero raw-debt objects reported and a byte-exact oracle-ordered hybrid. Inspected sinking source and detailed freeze boundary.
Three original-shaped C units with 90 functions and two TASM modules recovered, plus far-data/level codecs. Inspected configuration source and current matching-phase status.
Readable TP5 source and assembly for three episodes, including recovered level/actor logic. Per-episode reconstruction and generated host port are separately documented.
Lost 1995 author-source recovered from EXEPACK executable into structured QuickBASIC and a browser rendition. Native program models SAE MT-81 terminal and PLC-style process image.
Native pygame game with address-linked physics, damage, economy and AI reconstructed from static binary analysis; inspected projectile integrator.
Native game/service boundaries and executable-backed tables, with registered-v1.1 code/indirect-transfer inventory and gameplay parity ledger. Original EXE is validated/read as data, not executed.
Actual SDL2/Linux host adaptation of the Hocus Native game, despite stale Windows README. Inspected main.cpp SDL compatibility layer and Pyra-specific CMake backend.
Preserved source of Adam Lukers 2003-04 continuation of George Moromisatos Anacreon, with actual fleet/combat/AI/overlay units. Inspected structured ATTACK.PAS.
Native Python engine reconstructed from DOS game binary and converted world/art data; inspected original-address whole-word parser.
Original QuickBASIC executable recovered into QB64-PE source with rule/variable ledger and compatible save formatting; inspected main source and reverse-engineering notes.
Godot editor implements original map/resource/database formats using beyond-the-ire decompilation and roth_ripper/OpenROTH research; inspected native map resource parser.
ADF/DAX/graphics/map/ECL extraction and native Python interpreter for original event scripts; inspected ECL decoder and explicit rule-change ledger. Script VM is game bytecode, not 68000 emulation.
Modern Ghidra analysis extension, useful for compiled BASIC recovery but not itself a recovered historical game/application. Retain for a focused tooling pass.

README asserts complete reconstruction from screenshots/strings and broad assembly claims, but stronger behavioral or binary-derived correspondence is not established. Screenshots cannot certify complete functionality.

Screenshot-accurate modern Battleship recreation; inspected evidence does not establish original algorithm recovery beyond interface observations. Keep a qualified lead instead of repeating 100% validation claims.
README calls it a modern interpretation based on screenshots/string inspection. Original numerical behavior and binary-derived control flow remain unestablished; do not promote broad accuracy claims.
VWE arcade-cockpit 68020 interpreter and hardware research, not a native recovered Amiga/ST/CPC/DOS game. Secondary Amiga board mention does not establish the requested source-platform fit.
